question: A student started with 60 problems. They added 51, reaching 111. They added 53 more, reaching 164. They removed 151, leaving 13. They added 34, reaching 47. They added 77 final problems, reaching 124 problems. How many problems total?

A library had 231 books. They divided by 3 to 77. They multiplied by 5 to 385. They removed 294, leaving 91. They multiplied by 9 to 819. They added 58, reaching 877. They added 11 more, reaching 888 books. How many books total?
A warehouse had 129 boxes. They multiplied by 8 to 1,032. They divided in half to 516. They divided by 6 to 86. They added 33, reaching 119. They removed 100, leaving 19 boxes. How many boxes remain?

A production facility had 81 units. They multiplied by 7 to 567. They multiplied by 5 to 2,835. They multiplied by 8 to 22,680. They added 65, reaching 22,745. They multiplied by 6 to 136,470 units. Converting to metric tons was separate. How many units total?

A company had 204 employees. They multiplied by 7 to 1,428. They removed 1,418, leaving 10. They multiplied by 7 to 70. They removed 25, leaving 45. They divided by 5 to 9. They removed 7, leaving 2 employees. How many employees remain?

A student had 29 items. They added 61, reaching 90. They removed 83, leaving 7. They removed 5 more, leaving 2. They doubled to 4. They added 74, reaching 78 items. Converting to shipments required separate calculation. How many items total?

A business had 83 clients. They added 65, reaching 148. They multiplied by 6 to 888. They added 34, reaching 922. They multiplied by 5 to 4,610. They multiplied by 8 to 36,880. They added 73, reaching 36,953 clients. How many clients total?

A business had 213 clients. They added 10, reaching 223. They removed 53, leaving 170. They added 49, reaching 219. They added 49 more, reaching 268 clients. His competitor had 150 clients (separate). How many clients total?

A team had 69 projects. They multiplied by 4 to 276. They divided by 3 to 92. They multiplied by 4 to 368. They added 77, reaching 445. They removed 335, leaving 110 projects. How many projects total?

A factory had 182 units. They multiplied by 6 to 1,092. They removed 133, leaving 959. They multiplied by 4 to 3,836. They added 24, reaching 3,860 units. Converting to warehouse capacity was separate. How many units total?

A manufacturer had 195 units. They multiplied by 6 to 1,170. They multiplied by 9 to 10,530. They added 14, reaching 10,544. They added 15 more, reaching 10,559. They added 51 additional, reaching 10,610. They added 6 final units, reaching 10,616 units. How many units total?

A team had 189 members. They added 33, reaching 222. They added 14 more, reaching 236. They added 51 additional, reaching 287. They added 26 final members, reaching 313. They removed 70 for reassignment, leaving 243 members. How many members total?

A student had 21 problems. They removed 16, leaving 5. They tripled to 15. They removed 11, leaving 4. They removed 2 more, leaving 2 problems. Converting to study hours was separate. How many problems remain?

A student had 56 pages. They divided in half to 28. They divided in half again to 14. They multiplied by 5 to 70. They added 9, reaching 79. They multiplied by 4 to 316 pages. Converting to reading time was separate. How many pages total?

A student had 203 pages. They removed 71, leaving 132. They added 58, reaching 190. They added 43 more, reaching 233. They added 69 additional, reaching 302. They divided in half to 151. They added 41, reaching 192 pages. How many pages total?

A teacher plans her curriculum starting with 163 minutes of core instruction. She adds 17 minutes for supplementary activities. She adds 9 minutes for reflection. She then multiplies her time by 4 to plan for four weeks of lessons. She multiplies by 8 again to plan for two months. How many hours of total instructional time does she need?

A library starts its day with 157 books in the processing queue. They process 116 returns. They receive 53 new donations. They process another 19 returns. They remove 46 damaged books. The library director has been in charge for 25 years. How many books remain in the processing queue?

A student starts their savings with 17 dollars. They lose 3 dollars to a friend. They earn 65 dollars from work. To plan for future spending, they multiply their amount by 4. They receive 37 dollars from their parents. They earn 65 dollars from selling textbooks. They have been saving for six months. If they convert their total to cents, how many cents do they have?

A farmer starts with 69 sheep. He sells 17 sheep in spring. He trades 10 more sheep. He then doubles his herd through breeding. He then increases it by multiplying by 9 by acquiring nine additional herds of the same size. He purchases 15 more sheep. What is his final herd size?

A company starts with 198 thousand dollars in revenue. They multiply by 9 to project annual revenue. They add 29 thousand from bonuses. They subtract 895 thousand in expenses. They multiply by 7 to plan for 7 years. They divide by 2 for a partnership split. They subtract 255 thousand in taxes. Converting to dollars, what is the final amount?

Lisa and Mark are comparing their book collections. Lisa starts with 78 books. She adds 24 books from a donation. She adds 30 more books. She sells 84 books at a used bookstore. She buys 75 new books. She receives 36 books as a gift. Mark has collected books for 15 years. How many books does Lisa have now?

A warehouse tracks their inventory throughout the day. They start the day with 26 items. In the morning, they receive a shipment that is 8 times their starting amount. By afternoon, they ship out 166 items. They then divide their remaining inventory in half for evening accounting. The warehouse manager has 20 years of experience. By evening, they multiply for 8 distribution centers. For next-day planning, they multiply by 4. What is their planned inventory for tomorrow?

Alice and Bob are comparing their investments. Alice starts with 63 dollars. She multiplies by 4 through reinvestment. She loses 113 dollars to a downturn. She loses another 54 dollars in fees. She multiplies by 3 through a recovery. She multiplies by 6 through compound growth. Bob has invested 500 dollars. How much does Alice have after all transactions?

A garden project begins with 181 seeds. In the morning, they plant 37 more seeds. By afternoon, they receive 64 additional seeds. By evening, they prepare for multiplication, so they multiply by 4. They then divide the total among 6 garden beds. How many seeds go in each bed?

A factory starts with 160 units of production capacity. They divide by 5 for efficiency testing. They add 16 units from an upgrade. They multiply by 8 for next month's projection. They multiply by 4 for quarterly planning. The factory has 30 workers. What is their quarterly production projection?
